Shows your **Pentair IntelliCenter** pool panel (i5P, i7+3, i8PS, i10PS,
i10+3D) in Gladys through its **local protocol** (TCP, port 6681): no cloud,
no account, straight on your network.

> **Never tested with a real panel.** Not affiliated with Pentair.
> The integration follows the pyintellicenter library (MIT). A firmware
> update of the panel may change the protocol. ScreenLogic is not supported.

## What you get

One device per panel (identified by the unique name of its system, not by
its IP address), with, for each object the panel shows:

| Object                        | Features                                                            |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Body (pool, spa)              | Water temperature, heating set point, heat mode (list), heating now |
| Circuit (pool, spa, featured) | On / off (list)                                                     |
| Light                         | On / off (list)                                                     |
| Pump                          | Running, speed (rpm), power (W)                                     |
| Sensor (air, solar, water)    | Temperature                                                         |
| IntelliChem                   | pH, ORP (mV), pH and ORP set points (read only)                     |
| IntelliChlor                  | Salt (ppm)                                                          |

Plus a **Status** feature (connected or unreachable). Circuits that are not
featured (the unused "Aux") are not shown.

- Temperatures are in °C: a panel set to °F is converted exactly
  ((°F − 32) × 5 / 9). When the unit of the panel cannot be read, no
  temperature is published.
- The water temperature of a body is only published while it runs (pump on):
  stopped, the panel keeps an old value.
- A value that is unknown, empty, or 0 where 0 means "not available" (pH,
  ORP, salt) is never published.

Read every 30 seconds by default (15 s to 10 min, adjustable), one request at
a time, on one connection.

## Installation

1. Give the panel a fixed IP address in your router.
2. In Gladys, install the integration and enter the IP address of the panel
   (or its host name, optionally followed by a port).
3. Save, then add the panel from the **Discovery** tab.

The panel has no credentials: nothing secret is configured.

## Turning off (always available)

Choosing **Off** on a circuit (or a light), or **Off** in the heat mode of a
body, depends on no option, nor on a read or a command in progress (it ends
them and goes on a new connection), nor on a failed read, nor on the
configuration: right after a restart, it goes to the address of the last
panel read (kept in `/data`), and a stop not yet seen applied before a
restart is sent again as soon as the container starts. A command that
arrived before it and has not left yet is given up. Several stops clicked
together go in one write.

It succeeds when the read back of the panel shows it (for the heating stop:
the mode Off **and** no heating any more). Otherwise the answer says why, and
the stop is kept (in `/data`) and checked every 15 s (each panel address has
its own check) and at every read:

- **no address known** (no configuration, no panel read before): nothing is
  sent for now; the stop is kept in memory and goes first as soon as an
  address is known;
- **the panel does not answer** (3 s of tries, every 250 ms): tried again at
  every check (15 s), at every read that reaches the panel and when you click
  **Test the connection**; a stop that never left is never given up;
- **refused by the panel** (a code other than 200): written again after
  15 s, then less and less often (30 s, 1, 2, 4 min, then every 5 min),
  without end; a refusal does not count as a write;
- **not applied yet** (the panel does not show it): written again 15 s after
  each write, 3 times at most (writes the panel accepted), then held without
  new writes, which the status of the integration says;
- **without confirmation** in time (4.3 s): checked the same way;
- **heating stop shown but the body still heats** (the panel shows the mode
  Off but still reports heating): watched, nothing written again; normal
  during a cool-down, but after 2 minutes the status asks you to check on
  the panel (the mode Off written comes from pyintellicenter and was not
  checked on a real panel); when the panel gives no heating state, the
  status says so ("heating state cannot be read") and the stop stays
  watched.

The status of the integration says where each stop is: not sent yet, sent
and waiting for the read back, refused (with the code), held, still heating,
or watched. When the panel moves to a new address (the same panel read
there), its kept stops follow it.

A kept stop is let go when the panel shows it, or when a command of the same
setting clicked in Gladys after it (option on) left without a refusal of the
panel (no answer lets it go too: the command may have been applied). A new
click on Off writes it again and counts its writes anew. A stop kept in
`/data` before a restart is let go the same way, unsent, when such a command
of its setting left since the start (a `/data` slow to read is applied when
its read ends). Never by time. A command that left less than 30 s before
the stop and lands after it is countered by a new write. While the heating
stop of a body is not seen applied, its set point, turning its circuit on
and turning a circuit group on are refused. A body "heats" while its heat
mode is not seen Off **or** the panel still reports heating (unreadable
counts as heating).

## Turning on and heating (options)

Three options, **off by default**:

- **Allow turning circuits and pumps on**: the circuits that are not lights
  (pool, spa and their pumps, featured circuits). Turning on a pool or spa
  that heats (heat mode not seen Off, or heating still reported) also needs
  the heating option (its pump starts, and with it its heating). A **circuit
  group** ("Spa Mode"...) may turn a body on: it needs the heating option
  while a body heats or no body has been read yet.
- **Allow turning lights on**.
- **Allow heating**: choosing a heat source, setting the set point. A **spa
  is limited to 40 °C**, a pool to the ceiling of the configuration (35 °C by
  default, 40 °C at most). The bound is checked on the value written (a whole
  degree), after the conversion to °F when the panel is in °F: 40 °C =
  104 °F; the low bound is 4 °C (40 °F).

They are lists and a set point, never a switch: a "turn everything off" never
reaches them. Each command reads the panel again right before (identity,
objects, unit), checks the options again right before writing, leaves within
3.5 s or not at all, and succeeds only when the read back shows the value
asked ("sent, not applied yet" otherwise, then reads at 5 and 20 s). Commands
arriving together (a scene) go in one write. Also refused: before the
configuration is read, when another panel answers at the address, or when a
stop was clicked meanwhile.

## Good to know

- The panel is never read sooner than the interval: not by the **Test the
  connection** button, a Discovery, a reconnection to Gladys or a restart (the
  time of the last read is kept in `/data`). Only the reads that follow a
  command or a click on Off (5 and 20 s) and the checks of a kept stop (every
  15 s, reading only the objects of the stop) are an exception.
- A value older than 2 minutes is never sent again as new.
- The chemistry set points (pH, ORP), the pump speeds, light shows and
  schedules are read only or absent in this version.
- The Pentair app, the screen of the panel and its schedules may drive it
  too: the last write wins.

## Configuration settings

These are the settings Pentair IntelliCenter asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Your IntelliCenter panel | `section` | No | Shows your Pentair IntelliCenter pool panel in Gladys through its local protocol (TCP port 6681), without any cloud: bodies (pool, spa) with their water temperature, heat mode and heating set point, circuits, lights, pumps, temperature sensors, IntelliChem and IntelliChlor. Enter the IP address of the panel (give it a fixed address in your router), save, then add it from the Discovery tab. Turning a circuit or a heating off always works; turning things on and heating are only allowed by the options below. Never tested with a real panel. Not affiliated with Pentair. |
| IP address of the panel | `string` | Yes | An IPv4 address or a host name, optionally followed by a port (6681 by default). |
| Allow turning circuits and pumps on | `boolean` | No | Off by default. On: Gladys may turn on the circuits that are not lights (pool, spa and their pumps, featured circuits). Turning a pool or spa on whose heat mode is not Off also needs the heating option. Turning off works either way. |
| Allow turning lights on | `boolean` | No | Off by default. On: Gladys may turn on the light circuits. Turning off works either way. |
| Allow heating | `boolean` | No | Off by default. On: Gladys may choose a heat source and set the heating set point of a body (a spa 40 °C at most, a pool the ceiling below). Setting the heat mode to Off works either way. |
| Ceiling of the pool set point (°C) | `number` | No | The highest heating set point Gladys may write for a pool (35 °C by default, 40 °C at most). A spa is always limited to 40 °C. Checked on the value written, after the conversion to °F when the panel is in °F. |
| Refresh interval (s) | `number` | No | How often the panel is read, in seconds. |
| Language of the feature names | `select` | No | Used for the feature names of the devices added from now on, for the status texts and for the command errors. |

## How to install Pentair IntelliCenter in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: Pentair IntelliCenter appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/lm1lc3n7/gladys-intellicenter:0.1.1`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-intellicenter](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-intellicenter).

Pentair IntelliCenter requires Gladys `>=5.1.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

Pentair IntelliCenter is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core. It is published and maintained by [LM1LC3N7](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7), not by the Gladys core team.
